text.p: Amdahl Corp executives said Wednesday they expect to post a profit in the 1997 first quarter, with revenues up significantly from a year earlier but down from the 1996 fourth quarter.

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jack Lewis said in a conference call the company expects sales of its new Millenium machines to be up in the first quarter from the 1996 fourth quarter, but not enough to offset a decline in sales of its older models.
Chief Financial Officer Bruce Ryan said the company expects to "stay in the black" and be cash-flow positive in the first quarter.
He also said Amdahl expects 1997 operating costs to fall 6.0-8.0 percent from 1996.

Amdahl today reported a profit from operations in its fourth quarter but a net loss as a result of a restructuring charge of $40 million, or around $0.33 a share, to cover the cost of paring its workforce and trimming facilities amid a transition to a more service-oriented business.
After the charge, Amdahl reported a net loss of $33.8 million, or $0.28 a share.
Amdahl said it lost market share during 1996, with the processing power of its shipments essentially flat compared with overall industry growth of 35-40 percent.
The company executives noted the product shift to its new line of mainframe computing systems during the year and said they expect to recoup market share during 1997.
"Dollars (from sales) will be up considerably" in 1997, one of the executives said.
"In 1997 we expect overall operating costs to continue to decline," said Ryan.
Even including expected costs of the company's bonus and profit-sharing plan, Amdahl expects operating costs to fall 6.0-8.0 percent this year.
Amdahl shares were down 1/8 at 11-3/8 at mid-afternoon.

Ryan said the company had extended to January 1998 a loan from Fujitsu Ltd that was to have involved a payment of $80 million at the end of this month. Amdahl has a $65 million payment due in April related to its Trecom purchase. Lewis said the company saw sales increases in all of its major product lines in the 1996 fourth quarter, but the year as a whole was devoted to refocusing on its new business model.

"I think we've made some significant progress," he said. "It was unquestionably a dismal year financially...(but) we are entering 1997 with considerably more momentum and fewer obstacles than a year ago."

Lewis said in the conference call, "First quater revenues should be up significantly from first quarter a year ago," but company executives "expect to see reduced product revenues from fourth quarter to first quarter."
"We expect Millenium revenues to be up in the first quarter," but this is unlikely to compensate for a decline in sales of older products during the period, he said.
Over the past year Amdahl has evolved from being primarily a hardware manufacturer. Its services and software businesses now contribute two-thirds of revenues, he said.
